title: Consider full structural SQLite invariants for termal.sqlite validation, gated on a previous-production-DDL acceptance corpus
outcome: Follow-up from the tm-7p9z.1 final dual review (Codex Medium). Current boot validation of termal.sqlite checks required tables, per-table column-name sets (order-insensitive, five maintenance-added columns tolerated pre-maintenance), schema/authority markers, and embedded legacy shapes — all read-only before any PRAGMA/maintenance. It does not validate column types/notnull/defaults, primary keys, foreign keys, or index definitions, so a same-name/same-columns table with a foreign PK/UNIQUE/FK/index shape passes. The verifier declined to expand scope inside the legacy-removal bead because constraint/index fingerprinting across nine tables risks false-positive resets of developer state on semantically equivalent DDL history (the harm removed in that bead). If pursued: derive invariants from PRAGMA table_xinfo / foreign_key_list / index_list+index_info (not raw sqlite_master SQL equality), allow ALTER-vs-CREATE equivalent shapes, and gate the rule on an acceptance corpus of every previous production DDL (fresh-created and ALTER-upgraded variants) so no historically valid database is rejected; add wrong-PK/UNIQUE/FK/index rejection fixtures. No Beads IDs in code comments.
disposal_reason: NOT PLANNED (backlog triage w-930e4d333f07, 2026-10-05; Greg's approval via Engram::Advisor #293). P3/P4, never started, no holder or children, untouched since before 2026-09-21, not reliability, data safety or pilot. The record is kept; reopen or re-file if it becomes relevant.
